title: Getting started with EpiExposure
text: Introduzir o usuário ao workflow básico: da exposição ao modelo. DLNM não é só modelo — é estrutura epidemiológica define_exposure() define como exposição atua tempo fit_epidlnm() estimula relação exposição–doença
code: library(EpiExposure)  # carregar dados data("TargetSpot") # definir exposição (DLNM structure) cb <- define_exposure(   wx_long = TargetSpot,   vars = c("tmean", "vpd"),   lag_max = 85 ) # construir design matrix dat <- build_design_matrix(   wx_long = TargetSpot,   cb_templates = cb,   lag_max = 85 ) # preparar resposta dat <- prepare_response(dat, y_var = "severity", family = "beta") # ajustar modelo fit <- fit_epidlnm(   dat = dat,   model_engine = "glmmTMB",   family = "beta",   random_effect = "epi_id",   epiexposure_spec = attr(cb, "spec") ) hist(dat$y_model, main="Distribution of disease response", col="steelblue")

title: An epidemiological workflow for DLNM interpretation
text: Explicar o pipeline conceitual Aqui NÃO precisa de muito código Exposição tempo → Estrutura lag → Modelo → Interpretação DLNM como framework epidemiológico, não só estatístico por que epidemias têm memória temporal
code: title("DLNM basis for temperature") library(EpiExposure) library(dlnm)  sim_data$dpp = sim_data$dpp-1   t = define_exposure(   wx_long = TargetSpot,   vars = c("tmean","vpd","rain"),   lag_max = 85,   df_var = 4,   df_lag = 4,   fun_var = "ns",   fun_lag = "ns" ) t2 <- build_design_matrix(sim_data, t, lag_max = 85) t3 <- prepare_response(sim_data, y_var = "y", family_choice = "beta") y_df <- t3 |>   group_by(epi_id) |>   summarise(     y_model = first(y_model),     .groups = "drop"   ) dat_model <- left_join(t2, y_df, by = "epi_id") fit <- fit_epidlnm(   dat = dat_model,   family = "beta",   model_engine = "glmmTMB" )  summary(fit)

title: Understanding exposure-lag-response relationships
text: Visualizar superfície completa 👉 Aqui você explica: resposta depende de DOIS fatores: intensidade da exposição momento (lag) 👉 conceito importante: O efeito não é instantâneo — ele é distribuído ao longo tempo.
code: surf <- predict_surface(fit)  plot(surf) plot(surf, type="contour", main="Exposure–lag–response surface")

title: From statistical output to epidemiological interpretation
text: Reduzir dimensionalidade (interpretabilidade) 👉 aqui você explica: DLNM = alta dimensão → difícil interpretar redução permite visualizar: Efeito acumulado ao longo tempo
code: red <- reduce_effects(fit)  plot(red) plot(red$type, red$effect,      type="l", lwd=2,      main="Reduced exposure-response relationship")

title: Identifying critical exposure periods in epidemics
text: Descobrir períodos críticos 🧠 Discussão 👉 aqui está uma DAS PARTES MAIS IMPORTANTES Explique: Nem todos os lags são igualmente importantes. 👉 insight epidemiológico: janelas críticas períodos de susceptibilidade
code: crit <- identify_critical_lags(fit) barplot(crit$importance,         names.arg = crit$lag,         col = "tomato",         main = "Critical lag importance")

title: Simulating environmental exposure scenarios
text: Interpretar efeitos por janelas biológicas 🧠 Discussão 👉 Aqui conecta com biologia: pré-infecção desenvolvimento sintoma 👉 você traduz estatística → biologia
code: windows <- define_lag_windows(lag_max = 85, cuts = c(7, 21, 40))  sum_eff <- summarise_effects(fit, lag_windows = windows) boxplot(effect ~ window, data = sum_eff,         col="lightgreen",         main="Effects by epidemiological windows")

title: EpiExposure
text: plant disease epidemiology, environmental effects inherently dynamic, cumulative, time-dependent. However, traditional analytical approaches often rely arbitrarily defined temporal windows, can fragment continuous processes obscure critical epidemiological signals. EpiExposure addresses limitations providing tools explicitly account temporal continuity, lagged effects, biologically interpretable summaries.

title: Compare predicted outcomes between multiple exposure scenarios — compare_predictions
text: function supports deterministic comparisons uncertainty propagation. `uncertainty = TRUE`, predictions computed sample level comparisons derived simulated values. `output = "summary"`, central estimate computed median sample-based distributions, interval limits derived empirical quantiles (default: 2.5 **Important:** although traditional terminology might suggest "mean", central estimates summary outputs correspond *median* uncertainty propagated, ensuring robustness asymmetric distributions. `uncertainty = TRUE`, function always operates simulated prediction samples obtained `predict_outcome(output = "samples")`. Summaries computed : - central estimate: median - uncertainty intervals: empirical quantiles approach ensures coherent uncertainty propagation frequentist (simulation-based) Bayesian (posterior-based) models, avoiding incorrect analytic variance approximations.

title: Compute lag-specific decomposition of Exposure Cumulative Impact (ECI) — compute_ecilag
text: function returns: - `ECI_raw`: unweighted cumulative exposure - `ECI_weighted`: weighted cumulative impact model scale - `by_lag`: lag-specific contribution summaries lag-specific contribution computed : $$ \eta(x) = \sum_k \beta_k B_k(x) $$ $$ w_l(x) \approx \frac{\eta(x + \varepsilon e_l) - \eta(x)}{\varepsilon} $$ $$ contribution_l = x_l \times w_l $$ `center = TRUE`, central finite difference used; otherwise forward difference applied. function supports deterministic estimation uncertainty propagation. `uncertainty = TRUE`, lag-specific contributions recomputed across simulated posterior draws model coefficients. `output = "summary"`, central estimate computed median simulated distributions, interval limits derived empirical quantiles (default: 2.5 **Important:** `uncertainty = TRUE`, central estimates returned `ECI_weighted` `by_lag` based median simulated distribution. Uncertainty propagated using model-consistent sampling: - Bayesian models (e.g., `brms`, `INLA`, `bdlnm`) use posterior draws - Frequentist models use simulation asymptotic coefficient distribution summary outputs uncertainty, median used instead mean provide robust central estimate asymmetric distributions.
